title: Rillettes de Canard
subtitle: French potted duck with duck fat and thyme
excerpt: Rillettes de canard is a French potted meat preparation: duck legs slowly braised in duck fat until the meat falls from the bone, then shredded and packed into pots with enough rendered fat to seal it. The result is rich, spreadable, and keeps well. Serve at room temperature with bread and cornichons.
sourceNotes: Rillettes are a method of long, slow cooking in fat that preserves the cooked meat. Duck rillettes are closely associated with the Loire Valley and the Sarthe, particularly Le Mans. The technique was historically a way to preserve meat through winter.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in sealed pots before the fat layer is pierced. Keeps for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Scales well. Make in large batches and pot into small jars for gifts.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Rillettes must be made at least 4 hours ahead to set. They are better after 24 hours. Keeps refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

content.text: Rillettes are a method, not just a recipe. The duck is cooked slowly in fat until it falls apart, then shredded with two forks and packed tightly into pots. The fat that rises on top as the rillettes cool forms a seal that preserves the meat. Do not be alarmed by the quantity of fat used: it is the cooking medium, not all of it ends up in the final product.

Heat the oven to 150°C fan. Season the duck legs generously with salt. Melt the duck fat in a casserole over medium heat. Brown the duck legs skin-side down for 5 minutes until golden. Pour off most of the rendered fat (keep it for later).

Return all the duck fat to the casserole. Add the white wine, thyme, bay leaves, garlic, and juniper berries. The fat and wine should come at least halfway up the duck legs. Cover and cook in the oven for 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is completely tender and falling off the bone.
Lift the duck legs from the fat. Remove and discard all skin and bones. Using two forks, shred the meat into coarse threads: not too fine. You want texture, not a paste.

Strain the cooking fat, discarding the herbs. Mix enough fat into the shredded duck to make it moist and cohesive: start with 4 to 5 tablespoons and add more to taste. Season well: rillettes should taste properly seasoned, slightly fatty, and intensely duck-flavoured.
Pack tightly into small jars or ramekins, pressing down to eliminate air pockets. Pour a thin layer of the remaining fat over the top to seal. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours to set.

items.cause: Not enough fat was mixed in when potting
items.fix: The fat is both flavour and binder. Add more: the rillettes should be just moist enough to spread easily on bread.

items.cause: Under-seasoned, or insufficient salt was used during cooking
items.fix: Season the duck legs well before cooking. Taste and adjust when shredding: this is the moment to correct the seasoning.

content.text: Rillettes should be served at room temperature: take them from the fridge at least 30 minutes before eating so the fat softens. Serve with sliced baguette or sourdough, cornichons, and Dijon mustard. In France, they are a classic starter or part of a charcuterie board (assiette de charcuterie).
